newsitem.title: USA: AMCORE sees charge from Country deal.
newsitem.headline: AMCORE sees charge from Country deal.

text.p: AMCORE Financial Inc said Wednesday it has completed the acquisition for stock of Wisconsin-based Country Bank Shares and will take a $2.5 million after-tax charge against earnings related to the transaction after the deal is effective.
AMCORE has completed acquisition of Country, a bank holding company with assets of more than $300 million.

AMCORE will record acquisition expenses related to Country of $555,000 on its books in the second quarter. Country will record merger related charges on its books of about $1.9 million in the second quarter.
The Country merger charges cover data processing integration expenses, legal, accounting and investment banking fees and the closing of a duplicate facility in Belleville, Wis.
However, the total charge of about $2.5 million will not be fully reflected in AMCORE's consolidated earnings until they are restated on the effective date of the merger during the third quarter.

Last year, Country earned nearly $2.7 million. Since the acquisition was not finalized until the third quarter, the profits and assets of Country and AMCORE will not be reported on a combined basis until the third quarter. The transaction is being accounted for as a pooling of interests.
According to terms of the transaction, AMCORE issued 3.7959 of its common shares in exchange for each share of the 433,699 Country common shares outstanding, or a total of 1,646,278 shares.
The acquisition brings AMCORE's assets to more than $3.6 billion with 41 locations in Illinois and 13 in Wisconsin.
AMCORE previously announced a second quarter after tax charge of $1.3 million for expenses related to another transaction, the acquisition of First National Bancorp Inc.
